text:
marcus: Quick share — I ran a marginal-token payoff scan for the new 13B candidate (nova13b) across int8 / int6 / int4 on our longform and chat slices. TL;DR: int6 gives ~28% cost reduction vs int8 with <1.5% quality loss on short chat, but longform continued-genre completions show a larger gap (~4-6% metric drop).

anya: nice, can you paste the slice names and the primary metrics? which quality metric are you using?

marcus: used GTN-quality F1 (weighted), 90/10 long-form vs chat slices: 
```
Slices: chat_short_v2, convo-turns, longform_book-continues, summarization_open
Metrics: GTN-F1, BLEU-ish proxy, perplexity on held seed
Cost: $/1000 tokens using our runtime cost model
```

leo: can you share the numeric payoff curve? curious about marginal gains per $0.001 change in token price.

marcus: pasted snippet: 
```
Model    | Cost($/1k) | delta_cost | GTN-F1(chat) | GTN-F1(long)
int8     | 0.025      | baseline   | 0.860         | 0.812
int6     | 0.018      | -28%       | 0.847 (-1.5%)  | 0.778 (-4.1%)
int4     | 0.012      | -52%       | 0.803 (-6.6%)  | 0.702 (-13.5%)
```

marcus: From that, marginal token value (perceived product uplift) flattens after int6 for chat; longform users would notice regressions if we push to int4.

anya: did you run prompt-sensitivity? sometimes prompts with code/structured outputs regress more on int6 than natural chat.

marcus: yes — quick priming test on code-format prompts (n=120). int6 had a small increase in format errors (~2%), int4 jumped to ~9%.

leo: product question — for a hybrid routing policy, what's the recommended split? route chat_short to int6 with fallback to int8 on failures? or keep a fraction to int8 for high-value users?

sana: product POV: we should keep a small canary (2-5%) to int8 for GTN-tiered customers and for any request flagged as "high-precision" by the heuristics. Most chat can go to int6. Longform default should stay int8 for now.

marcus: propose policy draft:
- chat_short_v2: primary int6, fallback int8 if quality score < threshold or latency spike
- convo-turns: int6 primary, 5% traffic pinned to int8 for monitoring
- longform_book-continues: keep int8 for now; consider int6 canary on <1% traffic for replay evaluation
- summarization_open: int6 primary but run fresh eval on sampled outputs for extractive quality (weekly)

ops-bot: [deploy-calc] Run complete: policy patch queued to canary pool (canary id: c-2026-03-21-01). Metrics capture enabled: token-cost, latency-p95, gtn_f1_delta.

anya: love the canary gating. two asks: 1) add a small automated re-eval on production traces to detect category-specific regressions (tables/code/quotes), 2) add a per-route cost alert when spend delta > 15% vs forecast.

marcus: noted. I'll add a small replay job that samples every 30k requests and re-evaluates with the golden prompts set. Also enabling cost alert threshold.

leo: one more — for GTN/internal guidance, can we compute "break-even user value" i.e., how much product engagement uplift (in % points of retention or feature use) would be required to justify moving longform to int6? if not exact, give a heuristic.

marcus: quick heuristic: given longform token spend X and per-token cost savings ~0.007 ($/1k diff between int8->int6), you need ~ (cost_savings / unit-value-per-user) * scaling factor. I'll run numbers tomorrow and post a simple table.

sana: perfect. if that table shows >5% uplift needed for payback, we'll stall longform change and invest in targeted quantization (per-layer calibration) instead.

marcus: OK I'll push the detailed spreadsheet and the small replay job results by EOD tomorrow. will tag this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:

leo: thanks — this is actionable. also recommend adding a short snippet to the README for GTN so PMs understand the tradeoffs (cost vs. fidelity curve).

marcus: done — will drop the README blurb in the canary PR.

sana: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [canary-start] c-2026-03-21-01 is live on 3 nodes. Monitoring pipelines: ingest OK.
